title: Ryan Broyles Breaks the NCAA Career Receptions Record
question: When did Ryan Broyles break the NCAA career receptions record?
answer: Ryan Broyles broke the NCAA career receptions record on Oct. 15, 2011, in Oklahoma's 47-17 win at Kansas. His 57-yard touchdown catch from Landry Jones was reception No. 317, passing Purdue's Taylor Stubblefield, who had 316.
summary: Ryan Broyles passed Purdue's Taylor Stubblefield for the NCAA career receptions record in OU's 47-17 win at Kansas on Oct. 15, 2011. Here are the numbers.
body: Oklahoma receiver Ryan Broyles took over the NCAA career receptions record on Oct. 15, 2011, during a Big 12 game at Kansas in Lawrence. The third-ranked Sooners won 47-17 to improve to 6-0.

The record fell in the second quarter. Landry Jones found Broyles on a 57-yard touchdown with just under eight minutes left in the half, and that catch was the 317th of his career. It moved him past Purdue's Taylor Stubblefield, who finished his career in 2004 with 316 receptions.

Broyles was far from finished. He ended the afternoon with 13 catches for 217 yards, a new Oklahoma single-game receiving record, and added a second touchdown, a 43-yard score in the fourth quarter. The game left his career total at 326 catches, ten more than the old national mark.
Jones threw for 363 yards and three touchdowns that day, and running back Dominique Whaley rushed for 165 yards, so the record arrived in a thoroughly dominant Sooner performance.
For Sooner fans, the date is an easy one to remember: October 15, 2011, when an Oklahoma receiver became the NCAA's career leader in catches.
